simple.meaning: to flaunt , i.e. raise a flag ; figuratively, to be conspicuous
simple.inThisVerse: The selected word is tied to דָּגַל (H1713) in the Hebrew source text. Part of speech: v.
simple.whyItMatters: This word appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, so BibleIQ can compare how Scripture uses it across multiple passages.
simple.summary: דָּגַל (dâgal) means to flaunt , i.e. raise a flag ; figuratively, to be conspicuous First listed occurrence: Ps 20 6.

definitions.short: to flaunt , i.e. raise a flag ; figuratively, to be conspicuous
definitions.full: H1713. dagal [ דָּגַל ] verb look, bahold (Assyrian dagâlu , Lotz TP 131 ; Thes Rob-Ges MV SS De make דָּגוּל a denominative from דֶּגֶל = lifted up like a banner , or furnished with a banner , i.e. exalted, distinguished , AV RV chiefest ); — Passive participle מֵרְבָבָה דָּגוּל Song 5:10 looked at, conspicuous , according to Dl HA 40 . [ דָּגַל ] verb denominative carry, or set up standard, banner — Qal Imperfect 1plural נִדְנֹּל Psa 20:6 (Gr Che נָגִיל ; Bi נְגַדֵּל , after ᵑ6 ᵐ5 ; Now נִגְדַּל ; possibly נַגְדִּל ?) set up standard in battle, compare Dl Pr 61. Niph`al Participle feminine plural נִדְגָּלוֺת Song 6:4 , 10 bannered, supplied with standards , participle as substantive, of bannered hosts , compare De. דגן (√ of following meaning dubious; Late Hebrew דַּגֵּן Pa`el heap up etc. seems to be denominative; Ol § 215 b. 4 derives דָּגָן from דָּגָה , compare MV; We Skizzen iii. 170 inclines to regard דָּגָן as derived from proper name, of divinity דגן (compare דָּגוֺן ), as cereal from Ceres ).
